svg.text: Privacy boundary: what stays, what leaves, what the code forbids
This diagram maps onto gates, not promises: break any line below and ⑪ or tests/check-package.py turns red
① Always stays on this machine

g.text: All computation
Seven kernels: parsing, projection, transforms,
lateration, orbits, atmosphere, sky places, vault
Offline data
cities 2.08 MB / land 763 KB / countries 9.4 KB
shipped in the package, never fetched at runtime
What you type in
pasted coordinates, NMEA logs, site tables, obs
in memory only; ⑩ history writes one AES-256-GCM
envelope — no plaintext on disk; wipe in one click
Map
"Vector" mode renders the offline land outlines
and sends no tile request at all
Share links
⑨ deep link / QR carries lat, lon and zoom only
no device id, no history, none of your input
Bridge service
binds 127.0.0.1; a non-loopback bind is rejected
and every request re-checks the peer address
/api/iface
answers "loopback only?" and how many interfaces
no hostname, no MAC, no LAN address list
10 of 11 panels work with networking off
Only ⑧ may leave, and only after you allow it

svg.text: ② Only these four things ever leave

g.text: 1 · GeoIP lookup
Sent: one IP + the source name. Looking up your
own egress IP leaks a coarse location to a third
party — no tool can anonymise that, so it is stated.
2 · Online map tiles
tile.openstreetmap.org, tiles around the view centre
exclusive with "Vector", off by default
3 · Target of system commands
tracert/ping must send probes to what you query;
the tool's job is character whitelist + argv list +
shell=False, and a 400 before any process starts
4 · Browser geolocation
handled by the browser/OS; this tool forwards
nothing, stores nothing, shows the refusal reason
Shared preconditions
· Without the allow tap, allow_real_network=false
and every network entry returns offline_disallowed
· Upstream URLs come only from the built-in table,
with one placeholder: {ip}. A custom upstream_url
must contain {ip} and rejects loopback, private,
link-local and non-http(s) → no open relay (SSRF)
six sources in the page, five in the bridges
· Static files never carry a CORS header. Only /api/*
answers cross-origin, and only by echoing the
caller's own origin when it is on the allowlist
(null · hosted page · loopback) — never "*"

svg.text: ③ Forbidden by the code itself

g.text: Coordinate-like parameters refused
lat / lon / lng / latitude / longitude /
position / loc / accuracy,
plus alt / altitude / bearing / heading / speed
→ the bridge never learns where you are
No shell execution
os.system / os.popen / shell=True / eval / exec
checked by tests/check-package.py over the AST;
prose inside comments is not a violation
No telemetry
no analytics, no update check, no crash reports;
vendor/ is local Leaflet and qrcode.js only
No path traversal
static serving returns 403 for .., dotfiles, keys
instead of silently rewriting the path
No invented data
unparsed traceroute → 0 hops + the reason;
RTT below 1 ms stays an upper bound, never
interpolated to 0.5 ms; a null result stays null
Ambiguity is yours to resolve
"31.23 121.47" lists every candidate reading
with confidence instead of quietly picking one
No plaintext personal data
history · favourites · preferences · probe all
cross one AES-256-GCM envelope under one key;
with the lock down the page refuses to save

svg.text: Browser ⑪'s GEONET 104 gates include "privacyAudit: build every source URL from a fake position — none may contain 31.2304 or 121.4737"; both bridges self-test (Python 110 / PowerShell 202)

on whitelist, argv, loopback bind and per-request peer guard, the origin allowlist, path traversal, upstream constraints, parsers that invent nothing; tests/bridge-parity.py replays 41 live cases on both bridges
